overview: White recovers the c4 pawn with Bxc4 after 3.e3 and gets a healthy d4 centre; Black takes space on the queenside or hits d4 with ...c5 or ...e5. The usual game is a piece-play middlegame with an isolated queen's pawn or hanging pawns, positional rather than forcing.

white_ideas.idea: Bxc4, Nf3, O-O and Nc3, then e4 or an IQP/hanging-pawn middlegame
Meet ...c5 with dxc5 or Bxc4 cxd4 exd4 for an IQP with open lines

black_ideas.idea: Develop with ...Nf6, ...e6, ...a6 and ...b5 to gain queenside space
Strike at d4 with ...c5 or ...e5 to free the position

typical_structures.structure: IQP after ...c5 and ...cxd4 exd4, White with active pieces
Hanging pawns on c5/d5 for Black after ...c5 and ...dxc5-type exchanges

character.notes: Main lines 3...Nf6 4.Bxc4 e6 are even, open piece play without forced sharp lines; neither solid fortress nor forcing.

gambit.notes: White regains the c4 pawn at once with Bxc4; Black cannot hold it.

soundness.notes: Sound for both sides; a mainstream QGA line.

structure.notes: d-pawn and c-pawn exchanged, open centre with open lines for pieces; same as QGA anchor (Open).

approach.notes: Standard QGA line, played at every level including by strong players.

level.notes: Plans are clear (develop, regain pawn, IQP play) and theory is light; Intermediate.

sublines_that_differ.name: 3...e5
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 dxc4 3. e3 e5
sublines_that_differ.how: Black hits d4 at once; after Bxc4 exd4 exd4 White gets open lines and an easy game.

character.reason: Open piece play that is even and neither forcing nor a fortress.

gambit.reason: White regains c4 at once with Bxc4.

soundness.reason: A mainstream line sound for both sides.

structure.reason: Central pawns come off and pieces take open lines, as in the QGA anchor.

approach.reason: A regular QGA variation for strong players.

level.reason: Clear plans with light theory, not a first-repertoire line.

plans.reason: IQP and hanging-pawn structures with development lead are the usual themes.
